title: Cold rebuild: Keyset paging
summary: Rebuild Keyset paging from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Keyset paging** in *Pagination done right*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Two posts arrive while a reader is between page 1 and page 2. What does this print?
code: for (var i = 1; i <= 6; i++) db.Posts.Add(new Post { Title = "P" + i, Score = 0 });
db.Posts.AddRange(new Post { Title = "P7" }, new Post { Title = "P8" });
var keyset = db.Posts.OrderByDescending(p => p.Id).Where(p => p.Id < lastId).Take(3).Select(p => p.Title).ToList();
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=feed.db");
protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder model) => model.Entity<Post>().HasIndex(p => new { p.Score, p.Id });
steps.explain: Newest first, page 1 is P6, P5, P4. Two new posts push everything down, so offset page 2 repeats P5 and P4. Keyset paging asks for "older than P4" and continues exactly where the reader left off.

steps.title: Rebuild Keyset paging cold
prompt: The tests give you `FeedDb` with `Posts` (`Id`, `Title`, `Score`) and an index on `(Score, Id)`. Write
record FeedPage(List<string> Titles, int? NextScore, int? NextId);
FeedPage Feed(FeedDb db, int pageSize, int? afterScore, int? afterId)

returning posts ordered by **score descending, then id descending** (best first; for equal scores, the newest first). With no cursor (`afterScore` null), start at the top. `NextScore`/`NextId` are the last post's values when the page is full, or `null` when there is nothing more (a page shorter than `pageSize`, or exactly the last rows: fetch one extra row to find out).
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
FeedPage Feed(FeedDb db, int pageSize, int? afterScore, int? afterId)
record FeedPage(List<string> Titles, int? NextScore, int? NextId);
